parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is in the presentation layer. It should only map HTTP requests to application calls: take the route and body, hand them to OrderService and return the result. findOne() does exactly that. create() also checks the order invariant 'quantity must be positive' inline (`if (dto.quantity <= 0) throw new BadRequestException(...)`) before calling the service. This is a rule about what makes an order valid, not a check on the shape of the request. It belongs in the domain layer (OrderEntity or a value object), or in the application layer (OrderService or validation on the CreateOrderDto). Keeping it in the controller means other entry points that call OrderService.create skip the rule. Some teams treat this as ordinary input validation, which is why confidence is moderate. Still, coding a business rule by hand in the controller, instead of declaring it on the DTO or in the domain, puts a responsibility in a layer it doesn't belong to.
